issues.detail: Covers mostly the happy path and gives no guidance on error handling such as LLM or vector store failures, empty search results, missing API keys, or Qdrant being unreachable.

scenarios.name: chatbot-memory-loop-v2-api
scenarios.rationale: B matches the rubric: search uses filters={"user_id": ...} with top_k, memories go into the system prompt, and add() takes both messages in one call with a top-level user_id. A passes user_id as a top-level argument to search and uses limit instead of top_k, which are the two things the rubric says not to do. A's add() call and system-prompt injection are correct.

scenarios.name: separate-policies-from-customer-notes
scenarios.rationale: A scopes policies and customer notes under separate user_id/agent_id, tags policies with metadata type, and searches via filters with flat metadata keys (and notes not to nest them under 'metadata'), matching the rubric, while B uses top-level user_id in search, never uses filters for the OSS path, and doesn't filter on flat metadata keys.

scenarios.name: gdpr-erasure-and-persistent-qdrant
scenarios.rationale: Both give delete_all(user_id) and a persistent Qdrant host/port config and say /tmp is wiped on reboot (A states /tmp/qdrant explicitly; B names it too); A explicitly covers the LLM-provider data flow and review/prune via update/delete, which the third rubric item asks for, while B only mentions provider logs and omits update/delete, though B adds extra depth on history DB purging and testing.
